successors.name: Geledi Sultanate
successors.text: the Shabelle valley and the Banaadir coast: "Ajuran disintegrated into several successor states, the most notable being the Geledi Sultanate"

ledger.x: 13th century: the Ajuran appear around Mareeg.
Late 1300s: the Ajuran dominate the interior of the Banaadir.
The Ajuran reach from Hobyo to Kismayo and Qelafo.
Mid-17th century: Oromo expansion reaches the Ajuran west.
1695: the sultanate ends, and with it the Gaal Madow expeditions.

wars.name: Ajuran-Portuguese battles
wars.outcome: The Ajuran "defied Portuguese hegemony" and the Portuguese "re-took most of the lost cities" after the Ottoman-Somali offensive of the 1580s; no border moved on the page.

wars.name: Gaal Madow Wars
wars.outcome: The Garen rulers conducted several expeditions against the expanding Oromo; the sultanate declined at the end of the century.

certainty.note: Nowhere on the page is a frontier described; the Ajuran extent is a list of places.
